verdict.rationale: Twilio's Authy docs say it provides an SDK for common web languages so developers don't have to call the Authy API directly. However, a runtime probe of the same docs page records the verbatim notice that the Authy API is closed to new customers and will be fully deprecated, with Verify v2 as the successor, so new builders cannot use these SDKs. Missing for 10: SDK access for new integrations, a list of supported languages or SDK documentation, a non-deprecated programmatic surface, and independent hands-on evidence of using the SDK.
